phase_0.boundary_condition: The root XML element seals every directive inside one nested container so influence flows through containment and hierarchy rather than arbitrary links.

⊢.chosen_element: empty schema root before any directive is named
⊢.justification: The uninitialized document contains no elements and no steering state, matching the void initial object before anything is named.

⊣.chosen_element: closed root container that holds the full schema
⊣.justification: The terminal anchor closes the system and contains every directive as one register, matching the hermetic vessel seal.

≻.chosen_element: input trigger entering the schema from the user side
≻.justification: The forward morphism carries a trigger toward the steering target, directing behavior change through the signed interface.

≺.chosen_element: constraint feedback returning from the model to the schema root
≺.justification: The reverse morphism descends from observed behavior back to the container, carrying discrimination results inward.

⋈.chosen_element: chain of directive-effect pairs applied in sequence
⋈.justification: Composition links each constraint to its matching steering effect one-to-one, forming the sequential skeleton of the schema.

⊙.chosen_element: self-referential schema node that recognizes itself as the constraint
⊙.justification: Identity makes the boundary and interior one register so every directive inside the container is simultaneously the constraint itself.

∈.chosen_element: discrimination node that separates valid from invalid triggers
∈.justification: The co-multiplication opens one incoming trigger into two arms: one accepted for steering and one rejected as invalid input.

∋.chosen_element: recombination node that rejoins the processed arms
∋.justification: Multiplication unions the carried alternatives back into a single constraint register, reconstituting the schema state after discrimination.

⊤.chosen_element: affirmative steering effect that changes model behavior
⊤.justification: The constructive truth arm records that a valid trigger successfully redirected the model within the behavioral context.

⊥.chosen_element: negative rejection of an invalid trigger
⊥.justification: The constructive falsity arm records that an input failed discrimination and produced no steering effect.

⊞.chosen_element: contradictory trigger accepted and rejected at once by overlapping context rules
⊞.justification: Engagement holds both true and false simultaneously without resolution, keeping the paradox live as a Z2-protected boundary state.

⊡.chosen_element: append-only measurement record of fixed steering outcomes
⊡.justification: ROM fixation permanently stores each directive and its effect so the record cannot be undone or rewritten.

phase_2.split_input: incoming trigger from the disjunctive partner set ∋=𐑜
split_outputs: valid steering arm accepted by the discrimination node
invalid rejection arm refused by the discrimination node
phase_2.fuse_result: single constraint register holding the union of accepted and rejected outcomes
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: No schema exists yet; the document is empty and no directive, trigger, or constraint has been named.
phase_3.true_description: A valid trigger passed discrimination and its matching steering effect changed model behavior.
phase_3.false_description: An invalid trigger failed discrimination and produced no steering effect on the model.
phase_3.both_description: A trigger is simultaneously accepted and rejected by overlapping context rules, holding the contradiction live without resolution.

steps.domain_action: initialize the empty XML document root before any directive is named.
seal the root container so all directives sit inside one nested boundary.
make the boundary and interior one register so each directive is simultaneously the constraint itself.
accept an incoming trigger on the signed directional interface from the user side.
split the incoming trigger into valid and invalid arms at the discrimination node.
affirm the valid arm when the trigger matches the behavioral context.
refute the invalid arm when the trigger fails discrimination.
compose the accepted constraint with its matching steering effect one-to-one.
return constraint feedback from the model to the schema root through the reverse interface.
rejoin the valid and invalid arms into a single constraint register.
hold both acceptance and refusal live when overlapping context rules fire on the same trigger.
fix the steering outcome permanently in the append-only measurement record.
chain the next directive-effect pair in the sequential schema.
chain the following directive-effect pair in the sequential schema.
propagate the steering instruction across the entire model behavior with global correlation length.
anchor the completed schema as the terminal container that holds all steering directives.

phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Components communicate through containment and hierarchy inside the sealed root container rather than arbitrary links.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: State is stored in the append-only measurement record and retrieved from the resident history bank by message index.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The order of operations follows the CLINK chain of directive-effect pairs, with the discrimination node timing the split and fuse.
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical reference is the catalog at /home/mrnob0dy666/.imscrbgrmr/catalog.json and the bootstrap store is the tuple ⟨𐑦𐑰𐑩𐑿𐑞𐑤𐑲𐑜⊙𐑫𐑙𐑴⟩.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One trigger evaluation and one constraint-effect pairing per cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The schema root holds unapplied directives and the model waits for a steering input.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The measurement record contains the fixed outcome and the model behavior reflects the accepted constraint.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 - the cycle moves information between register and record without creating or destroying state.
